subject: QBR: Hedging capacity & unit-cost scenarios for upcoming quarter
summary: Leadership-level QBR prep thread: propose hedging (reserved capacity + spot burst), two run-rate unit-cost scenarios, and asks for numbers and final decision by EOD. Highlights: 1) model shows 18% reduction in tail spend with hybrid hedging, 2) batching and KV-cache delta included, 3) ask to approve runway commit for Dedicated pool and contingency to burst to partner cloud.
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR: Hedging capacity & unit-cost scenarios for upcoming quarter

Team —

I'm consolidating the infra section for the QBR (slot: Wed 6/30 leadership review). Main ask: we need a short, defendable recommendation on capacity strategy and the impact on per-token unit economics under two plausible demand curves for next quarter.

High-level hypothesis: a hybrid hedge (partial Dedicated reserve + spot/partner burst) reduces our 95th-percentile spend risk while keeping nominal committed costs manageable. I attached a working capacity model and a short set of scenarios. Key questions I want answered by EOD today so I can draft the slide: 

- Confirm the 2 scenario numbers in the model (base demand and surge demand).
- Quantify unit-cost delta (GPU $/token) with: (a) current batching baseline, (b) +aggressive batching, (c) +KV-cache hit at 20%/40%.
- Recommended commit level (GPU-months) for Dedicated to achieve target tail exposure under a 2x surge.

Attachments: qbr_capacity_hedge_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If we can agree on a concise recommendation (one slide), I will present the ask and the rollout steps (procurement triggers, fallbacks to partner cloud, SLO/observability hooks).

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: Hedging capacity & unit-cost scenarios for upcoming quarter

Jonas — thanks for the clear ask. A couple of firm asks from leadership side before we finalize the slide:

1) Make the recommendation binary and timeboxed — i.e., recommend X GPU-months reserved now with condition to re-evaluate after 6 weeks of telemetry.
2) Include uplifts to unit-cost that account for both reserved amortization and partner burst premiums (show blended $/token).
3) Call out operational risks & mitigations: pre-warming, KV-cache eviction risks, and fallback latency hit for partner bursts.

I've attached a short note format we prefer for QBR slides — use the top-row to state the recommended action and the second row for the measurable success criteria.

Attachment: QBR-slide-template (embedded in qbr_capacity_hedge_model_v3.xlsx)

Please incorporate Marissa's real telemetry numbers (not model defaults) and surface the worst-case tail spend (p99.9) as a residual risk number. I want a single sentence we can headline to the execs.

— Lauren
Director, Infrastructure Strategy
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: CloudVendor SRE <sre-ops@cloudvendor.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: Hedging capacity & unit-cost scenarios for upcoming quarter

On Mon, Jun 21, 2026 at 11:05 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jonas — thanks for the clear ask. A couple of firm asks from leadership side before we finalize the slide:
>
> 1) Make the recommendation binary and timeboxed...

Attached the telemetry extract and the sensitivity PDF. Key datapoints pulled from last 90 days:
- Observed mean GPU utilization per reserved slot: 58% (sd 12%).
- Peak daily 95th percentile of token throughput increased 2.4x on product launches; those events lasted 2–4 days.
- Current batching baseline avg: 1.9 requests/batch; aggressive batching experiment drove 3.8 reqs/batch at same p99 latency for non-chat workloads.
- KV-cache hit estimates: typical working-set = 17% hit, conservative scenario uses 10–20% for forecasts.

Model note: with a hybrid hedge of ~40% reserved + 60% burst capacity, blended unit-cost moves from $0.00053/token (hosted-only baseline) to:
- $0.00047/token (with aggressive batching + 20% KV-cache)
- $0.00061/token (if burst uses partner cloud with 1.5x premium and cache stays at 10%)

Attachment: gpu_unitcost_sensitivity.pdf (3-page) — contains the p99.9 tail spend chart and sensitivity table.

Action items I recommend we surface on the slide:
- Recommend 120 GPU-months committed for Q3 (40% of forecasted steady-state) with a 6-week telemetry re-eval.
- Approve a partner-burst budget cap equal to 25% of committed spend for surge days.
- Trigger pre-warm runbook to reduce cold-start latency during bursts.

I'll hand the cleaned numbers back to Jonas for the slide.

— Marissa
Senior Capacity Planner
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-21T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: Hedging capacity & unit-cost scenarios for upcoming quarter

Thanks all — this thread is great and concise.

Decision (for slide): Approve the hybrid hedge recommendation.

- Commit 120 GPU-months as proposed by Marissa (finance to draft reserve terms).
- Approve the partner-burst budget guardrail (25% of committed spend).
- Telemetry check-in in 6 weeks; if observed utilization >70% for reserved pool for 2 consecutive weeks, we escalate to increase commitment.

Jonas — please finalize the one-slide recommendation (headline + 3 bullets: numbers, risks, ops triggers) and share to #qbr-deck by EOD tomorrow so we can include it in leadership packet.

Karthik
VP, Infrastructure Operations
